utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sit down, please. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Poriouvaev:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you requested some protective measures, and your motion is granted by the Trial Chamber and so you will be given a pseudonym. You are called "Witness Q" now. So you will be called this way throughout the examination today, and you should not pronounce your own name. Now, you were given the sheet of paper. If you unfold it, you will see some name written on it. If it is your name, you should say, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Q, did you have any military background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I served one year in the Danish army, and then I served four or five years in the national guard in Denmark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any special military training in Denmark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I was trained as an infantry soldier in an armoured infantry company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever take part in any military campaign abroad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: In the Danish army, I never took part in any military actions abroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you: Did you ever take part in any military campaign?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I took part in the war in Bosnia, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did that take place? When did you leave Denmark, and where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I left Denmark in March '93, and I went to Zagreb to join the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you decide to join the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: It was due to idealism and also because I wanted to -- some adventure and to fight the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you have to do on arriving in Croatia in order to join the Croatia army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I went to a police officer on the street and asked him how to join the Croatian army, and he told me to go to a police station in Zagreb, where I was told to go to the Ministry of Defence. I went to the Ministry of Defence and was taken to another address by a HOS soldier, who took me to an address in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that HOS soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, we never talked about any names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: From there, I was taken to another address where I met up with some HVO soldiers. And I was interrogated by them, my motivations, my military background. And from there I was -- three days later, I was enlisted in the 106 Brigade in Orasje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was one of the HVO soldiers who talked to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: It was a soldier, an officer by the name of Blizanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you spell it for the record?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I'm not sure I can spell it, but I can try.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, try.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: B-L-I-S-A-N-O-V-I-C-H [sic]. That's what I think it was spelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: And then I was enlisted in the 106 Brigade in Orasje, north-eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a regular unit or HVO army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: It was an HVO army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regular unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Regular HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in command to that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: It was Blizanovic who was in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask you to go into private session just for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The point is that the witness may give a name now of a person who may be a potential witness, and his name should be protected at this stage, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive uniform, weapons, ID?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I received uniforms and weapon and ID. I received ID, but I don't quite remember where I got the ID, but I got an ID.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of uniform did you get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: A normal camouflage uniform with the HVO patch on the left arm with two crossing rifles and a checkered -- a red and white checkered back/badge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the name of the unit indicated on the patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. It was just stamped "HVO".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapons were you provided with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I was provided with an AK-47 Kalashnikov.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which currency did you receive your salary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: In that unit, I received my payment in Croatian dinars at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the functions of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The function of this unit was to guard the front line, the front line, the Serb front line, guard trenches and bunkers, patrol duties, but mainly guard service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you involved in any military operations while being in that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Not exactly. Mostly guard service, some patrol duties, but never any real military actions, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay within that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Approximately six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you leave it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Because nothing was happening. In this unit, nothing happened. It was too boring. We wanted some action, fight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I left with three other foreigners, and we went to Zagreb, and then we went to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you decide to go to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: We saw -- we did see in the television, in the news, that there was a lot of fighting going on in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Once again, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between whom fighting was going on in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Armija BiH, the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you decide to join the Croatian side or the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever been to Mostar before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, never. I have been in Yugoslavia before the war but never in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit Mostar after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was the first time that you came to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: It was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go in Mostar? Where did you find the unit in need?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: First we arrived at a checkpoint outside Mostar where guards, HVO guards, on the checkpoints asked what we were going to do in Mostar, why we came to Mostar. And from there, we were taken down to a headquarter somewhere in town where officers once again interrogated us, again about our motivations, military background, and so on. They were pretty suspicious. But after a while, we were accepted, I presume. We were then taken to a base somewhere in town, where a man named "Stela" was in command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the first time that you heard this name, "Stela"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: This was the first time I heard it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Once again, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him on that day? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Did I see him on that day?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, I did. We were taken to his office. The four foreigners of us were taken to his office and then, once again, interrogated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he very happy to accept you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, he looked like he didn't want -- he didn't want us in his unit. But I think we were only accepted in this unit because he had to accept us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he talk to you in his office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, that was in his office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you describe the area where that office was located and the office itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: It was -- I don't quite remember. It was an ordinary house in Mostar. I don't remember the colour of it, but there were several floors. And the office was about five metres long, three to four metres wide, a kind of small office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you hear the real name of the person who was called "Stela"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Sometime later on. I don't quite remember when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the unit you were accepted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, the unit was called "ATG Vinko Skrobo".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you understand by "ATG"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: "Anti-Terrorist Group".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they brief you on your future functions within the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you learn about the unit; background, its functions? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I later heard that the name of the unit was part of a battalion called "Kasniske Bojna", which stands for "Punishment Battalion". And I was also told that the unit and the members of the unit were all ex-punished persons during the Communist war in Yugoslavia, during the old Yugoslav. They were all ex-convicts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was Stela's superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I later heard that Stela's superior, the battalion commander, was Tuta, a man named "Tuta."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his real name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, I don't. I only know him as "Tuta."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know it now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: That was common knowledge. Everybody -- a lot of people talked about it and talked about Tuta, and talked about all the power he got, and actually people were quite afraid of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you get your accommodation within the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: My what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Accommodation, flat or barracks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Okay. The foreigners, the four of us, we received two flats about 100 metres away from the unit's headquarter. We had two flats. We emptied one of them and made one flat for us to live in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the local soldiers; where did they live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I don't really know. Some maybe were living in the building at the headquarter, maybe -- and some maybe also had flats out in the Croatian part of the town. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they brief you on your functions within the Vinko Skrobo Unit, your place of military service, your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No. I think three or four days after we arrived, we were taken to the front line, where the unit has responsibility -- an area of responsibility, and there we were shown the positions, enemy positions, what to do, how to do it, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could you expand a little bit more on this "what to do"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: What to do was mostly to do guard service once again, keeping the Muslim soldiers from taking our -- the building again through the line, to keep the enemy soldiers away from the line. But mostly again guard service. But there was a lot of shooting all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the area in which your positions were deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I remember one big concrete block which, before the war, I think, was a kind of a dental surgery building. On the top floor, there was a lot of, you know, like dental chairs, dental instruments, instruments surrounding -- which doctors use and dentals -- dentists. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I show you a picture of some part of Mostar, could you identify --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the usher to place Exhibit 14.5 on the ELMO. It's not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll point out the place?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This building and this one and this one were our areas of responsibility. This building, too, but there were no positions. It was just blocked off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any fortifications on the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry to interrupt. As for the picture, can you give some descriptions of the locations of which buildings?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's return to the picture now. So --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes. Our area of responsibility was in this building, which was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe a little bit this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: This building was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Its form, shape and --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: This building was a concrete building before, had been a dental surgery building or something like that. The other buildings, I'm not sure, but probably civilian buildings of some kind, this one and this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that you should take a pen and just mark all these buildings, Number 1, Number 2, Number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Number 1, what was in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: There was a position at the corner over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The building, in the corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: There was a position in the corner, yeah. You are facing the enemy with your back and looking into a mirror which overlooked the place in front of the building. And then --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: -- the second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the red roof, building number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Number 2, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you have on that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: On that building, there was some position, but they were not permanently occupied by -- in the basement, there was, like, a resting room for the unit. It was in the basement, and you were secure down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean this building with the flat roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yeah, with the flat red roof, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was there in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: There was also just a position, mainly a listening position where you just sit and listen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Put a number on it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Once again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Number 3, yeah. I just drew number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark it? So it's not the building with the flat roof; just the building on the opposite side of the street, also with a red roof.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this one, number 4. What did you do there in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I think that belonged to another unit, maybe it was a special Vojna Policija who was in this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was it your area of responsibility or the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I think that was the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In which building did you perform your duties, guard duties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: In building number 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were all these buildings and the confrontation line itself somehow fortified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The windows was fortified with sandbags and with holes to shoot through, you know. And some doors and some windows have been blocked so you couldn't go through them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But who did all these fortifications?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The fortification were already built when I arrived. Sometimes they were broken down by enemy fire and things like that. And when they have to put up new sandbags, it was mostly prisoners who were forced to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there firing on the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there sniping along the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I think so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Muslim side fire back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it dangerous to be on the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: It was dangerous if you popped your head out, or showed yourself to the enemy, it would be dangerous, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any prisoners doing some other job on the confrontation line apart from carrying sandbags and fortifying the buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I saw them -- I saw them working as a kind of waiter for the soldiers working on the front line, making coffee, bringing coffee, things like that, cleaning boots, weapons, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever witness -- eyewitness civilians crossing the confrontation line from the west part of the city to the east part of the city and vice versa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I saw -- doing guard, I saw mostly old people with all the belongings on their backs who was sent from the western side over to the eastern side. I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those people escorted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Once again, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all those people escorted by someone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yeah, they were escorted by HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of people -- I mean, the age, sex, did you -- you saw crossing the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yeah, it was mostly old people, both men and women, who were forced to go to the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecution, since we are talking about confrontation line, could you please be kind enough to show us where that confrontation line draws on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The confrontation line --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The confrontation line, at least that part that you saw, that you were present, and that you know that it was a part of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I know that everything in front of here was the confrontation line, and down here was also a confrontation line. I think it ran something like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the street where the confrontation line --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you give us a description, for the sake of the record --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. For the sake of the record, this street, the area that was shown by the Witness Q is that that is to the right side from the medical centre indicated by the witness as number 1, building number 1. So the confrontation line, according to this witness, is just to the right side along the street which name he doesn't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would suggest, if you agree, that the witness should draw this in the same way that he marked the numbers, that he draw it simply. It would be clearer than simply using words. THE COURT: That's a very good suggestion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you may try.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Okay. This is the confrontation line I know about. What's right and left of those, I don't know anything about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was your unit and military police the only ones -- I mean units, formations -- that were performing duties on the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I think there were several other units to our left and to our right, but which units they are, I don't know. But there were other units. It was a long confrontation line running through the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your unit and you, personally, involved in military operations on the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, we were. We tried to do one attack one time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly when it happened, but something like late August of '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of operation was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Couple of days before the attack, some officer I don't know and don't remember his name, came to us, to the foreigners, and told us there was going to be an attack. And that the attack would start with the artillery and mortar fire on the Muslim positions, and also gas would be -- CS gas would be thrown over the Muslim positions. And we would be supported by tanks and that the -- I was told that 10 to 15 prisoners would be -- would have a camouflage jacket on and be given a wooden rifle and act as a human shield during that attack. And the attack went on a couple of days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in command of that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I don't know who was in command. I don't know, but I presume that our commander, Stela, was in command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him the day of the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Yes, I saw him at the base area, but I never saw him on the front line, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean the base area, his headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yeah, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was he doing there, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Just running around, talking to people, giving them orders. I didn't talk to him that day, but I presume he was giving orders to his men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the man who was giving orders to you -- just before the attack, was there any preparation for the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The day the attack started, we met up at the headquarters, the unit's headquarters, about 2 kilometres, 3 kilometres from the front line and went on to our normal position. Then we waited in building number 1 at the right side of the building, facing the front line. Then we waited for the attack. And the artillery came, or mortars, I don't know, going on for some minutes. And then the tank came driving up towards the front line, and the tank started shooting. And we were ordered to attack, and we all went out with the prisoners in front of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, one moment. One moment, just apologise. And who was the man who gave you order to start attacking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: It was some officer in the unit. I don't remember. I don't know his name. It was just a man with a radio, a Motorola radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he from your unit, the Vinko Skrobo Unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The tanks started shooting and we were ordered to attack, and everybody ran out to storm the Muslim positions, with the prisoners in front of us acting as a human shield.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop, stop. Could you show the route which was followed by the tank on the same picture, in the same picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes. This is where we waited for the attack when the mortars and artillery were coming in. And the tank came up from here, this street. Normally there would be a sandbag here, but it was turned down to give room for the tank. And when the tank started shooting, we ran out from here and up here to -- we didn't get any further than this because -- due to heavy fire from the Muslim positions, so we were pinned down. We couldn't get any further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any persons with wooden rifles --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- during the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I saw two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Hold on for a minute. Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting. Before we go on to the next question, I believe that the previous presentation of the witness, showing where the movements took place, cannot be used for the record. Perhaps he could draw it and do it more accurately to show the movement of the witness in a clearer fashion, or else we will not be able to understand that movement. And from the point of view of Defence, I think this is a very important issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. What we need is a description of the attacking movements from --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: That's why I stopped the witness and wanted just to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm happy to hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But thank you, my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll try to draw the route. This was the place where we awaited the attack and where we were seated while the artillery were coming in on the enemy positions. Then the tank came up, and it was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Show --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The tank was coming up to this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Just mark it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: There. And when the tank started shooting, we were ordered to attack, going this route.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers from your side were involved in that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I would estimate it to be around 20, 25. And then the rest of unit were supporting us from the second floor in Building Number 1 with rifle and machine-gun fire, giving support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were there any people with wooden rifles, as you were told before that they would be involved in the operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: There were. I saw three people in a camouflage jacket, and they each had a wooden rifle, like a silhouette of a Kalashnikov. And those three people were sent out in front of the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them before the attack, before the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I saw them in the -- I saw them in the building where we were seated while the artillery were hammering on the enemy position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they sitting together with all of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the rifles they had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At close range?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Close or approximately five, six metres, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why do you think that the rifles were wooden?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I could see, I could tell it. They didn't look like my own Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. rifle. It was made from wood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you show me the way - again in the picture - these people were following during the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The same route as I just drew, from here out there in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You mean the front of the Building 1?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Building 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Building 1, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Those three persons with wooden rifles, did you see them before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Maybe. I don't really know. I think so, yes, but I can't tell it for sure right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know from which unit they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, I don't know. They were -- what I was told, they were Muslim prisoners there with civilian clothes. Whether they were prisoners of war from the army of BH or just civilian Muslims, I don't know, but they were prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they moving in front of the rest of the people involved in the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yeah, they were moving in front of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: They were moving in front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: In front of the unit, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of you. What --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: They were the first to go out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the distance between you soldiers and the people with wooden rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Just in front of us a few metres; three, four, five metres, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there shooting on the confrontation line at the time they were moving towards AB positions, AbiH positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: As soon as we -- as soon as we came out in the open area, the shooting started, a lot of shooting. There had been sporadic shooting all the time, but when we came out in the open area, there was a lot of shooting with rifles, RPGs and probably also machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you succeed to get to Muslim positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, not at all. We only reached -- we only got as far as you can see, the building in the photo there, so more in front of Building Number 1. That's the place we -- we didn't get any further, due to the heavy fire from the enemy side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to people with wooden rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No. I lost all eye contact -- I lost eye contact with those prisoners as soon as we came out in the open area. I was -- I was only thinking about the enemy fire and shooting back myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did foreign soldiers take part in that operation as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about another Danish soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: There was another Danish soldier, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he involved in the operation as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: He was involved. He was in the attack, just as me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the overall operation on that day successful?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, not at all. The operation, it lacked overall command. There was no -- there was no structure in the attack. It wasn't a success, not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there casualties from your side as a result of the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Until now, no, there wasn't any casualties. But after we pulled back, there was a casualty, a Danish guy -- another Danish guy. He was wounded in the arm from shrapnel, mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay within Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Two or three months, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I don't exactly remember when I left, which month, which day. But certainly me and another Danish guy, we went off to Tomislavgrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you decide to join another unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We went to Tomislavgrad, where we found a lot of other friends working for the Croatians. We stayed there, I don't know how long. And nothing went on, so we went to Ljubuski and joined up what we found out was another ATG unit from the Kasniske Bojna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I think the name was Zeljko Bosnjak, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What had you known about that unit when you were joining it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I found out that the infrastructure -- the lack of discipline was even worse than it was in Mostar. There was no discipline, nothing, and it was hard to tell if there was any infrastructure in the unit. It was just people with guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in command of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I think the commander of the unit was a guy with the name "Marko".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To which structure did that unit belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Also to the HVO, the Kasniske Bojna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: They told us that they were also an ATG unit, part of the Kasniske Bojna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean -- whom do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: "They," the Croatian soldiers, told us from the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was in command of Kasniske Bojna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The overall command of Kasniske Bojna was a guy named "Tuta."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yeah, I saw him in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did it happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when it happened, but I remember I saw him in Siroki Brijeg. When, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us a little bit about the circumstances in which you saw Tuta, and could you describe the man you call Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The man I called Tuta, he didn't appear as a soldier. Actually, he more looked like a hippie from the '60s with long hair, glasses, civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to him --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I talked to him once, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, that was during another episode in Ljubuski. Some guy from the unit has been killed by -- in town by I don't know who.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Soldier from your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: From the Kasniske Bojna, yes. And the whole unit was sent out to block the town so nobody would get in, nobody would get out. And we stood guard around the city for an hour, maybe two. And then suddenly, we were all sent up in trucks and cars and driving out to search and attack and search Croatian police stations in the search for this man who has shot this soldier from our unit. And that was the time when I talked to Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Outside some police station. I don't know where, we were just driving around on the lorry, on a truck, you know. I didn't know where we were, the circumstances. But it was outside a Croatian police station which had been attacked by this unit. Me and the Danish guy were driven around in this truck. We didn't even have a weapon. And what was going on, we didn't know exactly. And I saw Tuta and went to him and asked if we could just at least -- if he could at least give us a weapon, just to protect ourselves. We didn't know what was going on. And he told me in German, You want me to take another rifle from a Croatian and give it to you, or what? And we just looked at him and went away again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you doing in Siroki Brijeg when you first saw Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I don't really remember what I did there. Maybe it was when we were trying to sign up with this unit. We were given a bed in Siroki Brijeg at Tuta's headquarters just for a night. I think that's when I saw Tuta the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you enter the police station in Ljubuski during these, let's say, operation --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, I was only outside the police station, but close to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they find the soldier they were looking for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I think so, yeah. That's the rumours I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I think he would have been killed, shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Rumours, again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Rumours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I heard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I left the unit -- I left this unit, it was about Christmastime, December '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go back to Denmark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Then I went back to Denmark, yes, for a period of time, and later went back to Croatia again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any specific incidents which happened during your service within the Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I certainly remember the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the attack.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I remember once we were all told to show up at the headquarters, Stela's headquarters, and we waited with weapons. We didn't really know what was going on, if we were going to attack somewhere, something, or what. And there was a lot of soldiers there. And suddenly, all of the soldiers jumped into civilian cars, very fast, driving from us very fast, and we didn't even have time to get in one of these cars, me, the Danish guy, and some other foreigners. Okay, that's fine, we said. We went back to our flat and watched some television. And when the unit came back, two of the German volunteers who had been with them told us that they had been out in civilian Muslim houses confiscating VCRs, TV sets, stereo, et cetera, expensive items.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever eyewitness any mistreating of prisoners by --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Vinko Skrobo soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: By Vinko Skrobo soldiers? Not exactly from any Croats, except from they were humiliating the soldiers. But no physical abuse except from I saw one episode, this German, one German was beating up a prisoner in the cellar at the headquarters in Mostar, Stela's headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The name of him?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The name of that soldier was Aldeberg Schroder. He was from Berlin, Germany.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he punished for that mistreatment of a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I don't know, and I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why don't you think so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I never heard about it. I don't know if the commanders in the unit heard about it, but I don't think he was punished for it, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was any of your soldiers ever punished by your commanders --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- for wrongdoing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, we wasn't. Only one episode, this Aldeberg was punished. I think he was sent home, sent back to Germany, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: There was an incident in our apartment, flat, this Aldeberg Schroder, which had a serious alcohol problem, he was drinking a lot, he showed up with a little Muslim kid. I think it was a Muslim kid with no parents, very alone. He showed up with this kid in our flat and said he's going to live here. And the other guys and me, we protested against this and said, no, he's not going to live here, we don't want that, et cetera. The kid went off again. But occasionally, he showed up in the flat just watching television, drinking soda, and having a good time, it looked like. And it was all right with all of us, and he came once in a while. But one time I was sitting on the settee, one officer or a soldier from the unit, he came to me and said, Hey, you better go home, there's a kid who has been killed in your apartment. And we went home. And this Aldeberg Schroder was sitting at the headquarters, looking very depressed. And I don't know what happened, but maybe this kid was playing around with a hand grenade and it exploded, and he was killed in the apartment. After this, Adolf -- we call him Adolf-- Aldeberg Schroder was sent home, I think. That's the only punishment I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you describe the person that was known to you as Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: He was rather short, heavy-builded, short hair, kind of a pulled-up type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look around the courtroom, you will be able to identify some people who are familiar to you before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, I can point out Stela, who is sitting over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, please, don't hurry. Don't hurry. Indicate the place he is sitting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: He is sitting over there in the black suit, second from the left, in the behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No. There's no other one I can identify at this moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: That's all. My direct is over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall be cross-examining this witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Krsnik: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. I'm the accused Naletilic's counsel, and I will ask you some questions. If you will be so kind as to tell me how many statements have you given about the events and your experience in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I have given two statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the first statement was to the authorities in your country; that is, you made the first statement to the police in your country. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they summon you and ask you to make a statement, or did you volunteer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I volunteered for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went to the police station, and you said -- and told them that you would like to tell them something. Is that how I should understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I don't quite remember, but could be possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you waited for six years to remember to go to the police and tell them about your experience in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Nobody ever charged you with anything. Is that correct, I mean, the authorities in your country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No. No, nobody accused me of doing anything. And it's true I waited for some years, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please answer: Why did you wait so long to tell about the things that you went through? And did you know -- after you left Bosnia-Herzegovina, were you abreast of further developments there? Did you know what went on there after you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand the last bit of the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My second question -- the second part of my question was: After you left Bosnia-Herzegovina and went back to Denmark, were you aware of things that went on in Bosnia, and especially did you know anything about the fate of people that you testified about today after you left Bosnia? Did you keep in touch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, I only knew what happened in Bosnia after I left from the media, from the news, et cetera, and I didn't stay in touch with anybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did you then learn from the media or did you perhaps follow the proceedings at The Hague through the media?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: What do you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean did you follow what the media -- the media coverage of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the interpretations.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I did follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please re-ask the question and the two questions before, because you asked two questions and we missed the second question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the question before this one was whether the witness was aware of further developments in Bosnia after his return to Denmark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The first question you asked was: Why did he wait so long? And then you went into the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why, yes, and I think that after that -- I'll just check it, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. My colleagues, who are following the transcript and my questions, told me that first I was not given an answer, why did he wait so long. That is right. Why did he wait so long to go to the police? And then followed the questions about whether he was kept abreast of the developments in Bosnia. And my final question was: Did he follow the media in the coverage of this Tribunal? So I think these were my last three questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Before we got to that, and I'm following the transcript, you asked a two-part question. And before this witness had an opportunity to answer the first part of the question, you concentrated on the second part. So if we take the question, in fairness, bit by bit, the first question is: "Why did you wait so long?" And when you have the answer, then, if you want, you can ask him the further question about keeping abreast of the events in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. Thank you for your help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So will you please answer my first question? Why did it take you so long? Why did you wait so long to report or, rather, to go to the police in your country, if you had something to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Why I waited so long? Because I think when I first came home, I was just trying to find myself, find my old self again in the civilian -- in the civilised world. That's the only reason I can give you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you needed six years for that, to find yourself again and all Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that you told us, you needed six years for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I don't know if -- how long a time I needed, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Will you now answer my second question? Did you follow further developments or did you have any personal knowledge of things that went on in Bosnia after your return to your country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: After I went back, the only -- the only thing I knew about what was going on was from the media, from the news, the Danish news and also the international news. No personal knowledge of what was going on, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the media in your country, did you follow their coverage of the work of this Tribunal, I mean who are the accused, what goes on? Were you curious? Did you want to know what went on here? Did you follow that in your country's media?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I followed it in the media, yes. If I was curious, I don't know, but I followed it, as everybody else did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in the statement that you gave to the authorities in your country, that is, to the police, were you cautioned at the beginning of your statement that that statement could be used against you? Was that the case? Is that accurate, what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you nevertheless volunteered your statement without the assistance of a counsel or a legal advisor; you nevertheless wanted and insisted on giving such a statement, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the statement that you gave to the police in your country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that you never once mentioned somebody -- a certain man called "Tuta"? There is not a single word about it. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes. I never mentioned "Tuta" in the first statement to the Danish police, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you then be so kind as to answer me: How did you establish contact with the investigators of this Office of the Prosecutor? I'm using the acronym "OTP", which means the Prosecutor's team in this Tribunal. How did you establish contact with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: They -- they established contact with me. I guess the police -- the Danish police sent my statement down to The Hague, and after some time two police officers came to Denmark and interrogated me, asked me questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two Danish policemen came, if I understood you properly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, it was two policemen from this -- from this Tribunal, one Portuguese and one American policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there are no policemen in this Tribunal. It doesn't have any police force. Don't you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that. But two investigators, claiming that they were coming from The Hague, came to interrogate me. As I said, one Portuguese and one American.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they introduce themselves as policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you gave your statement, you thought you were talking to the police of this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Whether they were police from this Tribunal, I don't know. They identified themselves as police. One was an ex-policeman from Portugal and one was an ex-policeman from the United States of America.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I think my question is quite clear. When you gave your statement, you thought that you were giving it to the police; is that correct? That was my question originally, so I'm repeating. How did you feel? What did you think? Did you think that you were talking to the police or somebody else? This is very clear. We're trying to explain here as many things as we can. I believe we understand one another.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, we do. I talked to two policemen which I thought were working for this Hague Convention. All I know, they were policemen. They told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if my sight serves me well, it is 4.00, so perhaps I should continue my cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, are you cold? I was about to ask you - and this is my last question - are you cold? Are you feeling cold?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good, good, thank you. Yes, I would end there at this point, Your Honours, today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
